note: Practitioner history connects prefabrication, construction organization and industrial change. The full subtitle identifies historical explanation and future production, not primarily engineering procedures; no H3 established. Different production arrangements offer transferable constraints. Evidence is limited to professional description and syllabus use, so all quality estimates are low confidence; course adoption alone is not exclusion. No thematic or period deduction.

Twelve failed technologies test generalizations about adoption, performance, institutions and consumer behavior. Different failure causes add real learning and strategic transfer; not technical training. Three-century comparisons have no one central historical period; technology is central even when a nuclear bomber is a case. Neither thematic deduction.

Contents develop fractal geometry through constructions, iterated-function systems, rendering, dimensions and increasingly advanced fractal classes. Main mathematical learning sequence develops technical proficiency. Applications, illustrations and accessible prose do not override the curriculum exclusion.

Distinguishes forms and uses of ignorance across institutions and eras. Comparative cases add knowledge about concealment, specialization and limits of knowing; mechanisms offer transfer beyond a collection of curiosities. Broad history rather than a single period; no dominant thematic deduction. Quality confidence low because only description and scope inspected.

author: Phillip Lopate (editor)
note: Nonfiction personal-essay anthology, not fiction or a writing-skills manual. Reflective distinctions and general observations prevent a high-confidence claim of no transferable payload, but mechanisms, integration and domain fit are weak. Varied essays add literary knowledge; long personal detail lowers useful density for this reader. Collection first issued 1994, spans periods with no central historical endpoint. No additional thematic category established for the whole anthology.

Publisher's full description and chapters 9–15 make Christian Passion and revelation the explanatory key that breaks the universal cycle of sacred violence. This is not merely incidental history of religion; defense of a religious interpretation is central, establishing V8. Counterfactual E/M remain limited by extrapolation from selected texts. Distinct myths add comparisons; religious philosophy central, T12 applies. French original 1982; translation/reprint does not reset age.

Literary criticism applies mimetic desire to Shakespeare's plays and poems. It is nonfiction about fiction, not H2, and not a dramatic-writing course. Different plays supply interpretive comparisons, but selected literary evidence cannot independently establish universal psychology; reduced E/M. Philosophical interpretation central, T12 applies. Not a history of one period, so Shakespeare's dates are not used for H13. Original 1991, not 2004 reissue.

author: René Girard; Cynthia L. Haven (editor)
note: Selected writings span imitation, desire, rivalry, violence, religion and culture. The inspected description does not establish doctrinal truth as the dominant purpose of this whole anthology; no automatic V8 from another Girard book. Wide extrapolation from interpretive examples lowers E/M; no high-confidence V9 decision made without sufficiently specific critical evidence. Philosophy central, T12 applies. Original UK selection 2023, US edition 2024; no historical endpoint.

Comparative history of belief across eras rather than a devotional program or central claim that particular doctrines are true. Concise differences among traditions add learning; broad overview limits mechanisms and domain fit. General readership, not established primarily precollege. No single period or nation; religious history is not automatically philosophical truth assessment.

Dirac memorial lectures develop specialist arguments about spin/statistics and the relation between relativity and quantum mechanics. Formal physics argument is the main intellectual payload, requiring technical study. Distinguished authors and accessible prose do not override H3.

Intellectual history connects science, toleration, religion and ideas of happiness across Europe. Multiple debates add substantive context despite exceptional length; no direct density audit. Philosophical ideas central, T12 applies; historical treatment of religion is not V8. Explicit endpoint 1790. Original UK 2020 precedes 2021 US edition.

Portuguese expansion connects navigation, maritime logistics, trade chokepoints and coercion. Distinct expedition constraints supply transfer beyond explorer personalities. Portugal-centered conquest warrants both thematic deductions. Main early empire-building arc ends around 1515; H13 capped. Narrative history, not navigation training.

author: Seneca; John Davie (translator)
note: Collected essays chiefly offer consolation, management of anger, happiness and tranquility. Life-support guidance predominates despite an earthquake essay; the explicit Marcus Aurelius exception does not extend to Seneca. V7 counterfactual retains useful practical distinctions but limited empirical grounding. Philosophy central, T12 applies. Approximate composition endpoint 65 CE, low year confidence, gives capped P14; 2007 translation does not reset age. Timeless practical arguments, H13 zero.

author: Steven Novella; Bob Novella; Jay Novella
note: Past forecasting errors and technical constraints inform future technology scenarios. Comparisons can improve calibration; forecasts remain less durable than established mechanisms. Not a specialist training course and no hype veto established merely from future orientation. Technology central, no thematic deduction. Original 2022, later paperback 2023.

Fifty artworks are linked to movements, themes and historical context. Nontechnical art-history survey rather than instruction in producing art; substantive contextual explanation supports eligibility beyond a locator reference. Many distinct works add knowledge but little transferable mechanism or target-domain value. No central period or country; low score is retained rather than inventing V3.

Comparative history links legitimating ideas, property institutions and inequality. Different regimes and quantitative comparisons add learning, while very broad causal interpretation and length lower E/D estimates. Proposed redistribution is not in itself V5, V6 or ideological capture. Political-economic power central, T12 applies. Broad cross-period account with present implications; original French 2019 precedes English 2020.

Transport, production, culture and political transformation explain Europe from 1648 to 1815. Material and institutional connections support transfer and justify many distinct cases. Political transformations anchor the narrative, T12 applies; transnational scope avoids T11. Explicit period endpoint 1815.

Scientific group biography traces quantum discoveries amid war and displacement. Scientific-biography exception prevents V3; historical explanation rather than technical derivation prevents H3. Personal episodes and familiar physics reduce learning yield for this reader. International scientific work central, no thematic deduction. Approximate first-half-twentieth-century endpoint 1945; German original 2021, English 2022.

Quantified food systems connect production, energy, waste, dietary requirements and planetary constraints. Main purpose is system explanation, not a personal nutrition plan; no V7. Distinct supply and waste mechanisms support density and strong transfer. Environmental and resource-sustainability questions predominate enough for T11; production central, T12 zero. Present global system, H13 zero. Author's working-title wording How Food Really Works noted as an alias, not a second book.

Molecular aging, evolutionary tradeoffs and longevity research are explained and critically assessed. Main scientific inquiry is distinct from a personal longevity program, so V7 is not inferred from publisher health framing alone. Different mechanisms add learning; speculative interventions receive less confidence. Disease/death and longevity focus warrants T11. No closed historical period; original 2024, cited paperback 2025.

General-reader history explains discoveries and changing scientific questions. Publisher explicitly addresses curious readers of all ages, insufficient to establish a primarily precollege H5 gate. Varied discoveries add factual learning; familiar elementary material lowers utility and fit for an expert. No technical curriculum, single period or thematic deduction.

Distinguishes forms of corruption and their different relationships with investment, growth and political access. Typology and institutional mechanisms transfer beyond the Chinese case; not partisan mobilization. Different corruption types add analytical yield. China-centered political power warrants both deductions. Contemporary comparative argument, no fixed historical endpoint. Original 2020, 2021 paperback.
